entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Petitioner has filed the instant petition challenging communication dated 23.06.2020 issued by the respondent No. 3 to respondent No. 4 by virtue of which the respondent No. 3 has asked respondent No. 4 to stop vehicles carrying livestock (mutton) without license issued by the respondents No. 3.
02.

It is the case of the petitioner that after coming into effect of Food Safety and Standard Act,
2006, by virtue of Section 97 of the said Act, all enactments and orders issued under the Essential Commodities Act relating to "Food" stands repealed and the designated officers have been appointed in the Union Territory of Jammu and Kashmir to be Incharge Food Safety administration for each area including for grant of licenses, for wholesale as well as retail business of "Food".

Learned counsel has submitted that "Food" includes within its definition mutton and as such members of petitioner association have obtained license for running the business of mutton from the appointed designated officers.

Inspite of this, respondent No. 3-Department which, prior to coming of the force of Food and Safety and Standard Act, was the authority for grant of license for the aforesaid purpose, is interfering with the business of the petitioner association inasmuch, as it has issued the impugned communication thereby stopping the import of the livestock at Lakhanpur (Kathua).
03.

entities.text: Food and Safety and Standard Act
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the respondent No. 3 has submitted that inspite of coming into force of the Food Safety and Standard Act, 2006, SRO 646 dated 19.12.1973 which governs the matters relating to the licensing of the dealers/brokers and wholesalers of the mutton continues to be in force because fresh standards are yet to be prescribed in this regard.
The learned counsel has referred to Section 98 of the Food Safety and Standards Act in this regard.
04. Petitioner has placed on record copy of the SRO 646 dated 19.12.1973 (Annexure-II).

Clause 3 of the said SRO provides that business of mutton as a wholesaler, broker or a retailer cannot be carried out except under and in accordance with a license issued in this behalf by the Licensing Authority.

Learned counsel for the petitioner has contended that even if it is assumed that SRO 646 continues to have application, still then there is no bar to the import of the livestock as no license is required for import of livestock under the said SRO.

In this regard, he has relied upon the judgment of this Court rendered in OWP No. 762/2013 titled Chinar Sheep and Goat Suppliers Welfare Association and Ors. Vs. State of J&K and Ors. decided on 24.10.2013.

entities.text: Chinar Sheep and Goat Suppliers Welfare Association and Ors. Vs. State of J&K and Ors
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the said judgment, the Division Bench of this Court has clearly observed that in terms of the Clause 3 of 1973 notification import of livestock without license does not become illegal, its sale without a license is illegal.
05. Having regard to the submissions made by the learned counsel for the petitioner, a case for grant of interim indulgence at this stage is made out.

Accordingly, till next date of hearing, there shall be stay of the impugned communication dated 23.06.2020.
06.
List as above.
